lines.text: We came down that hill like an avalanche of our own. Oswin in front, Ash beside him, and Halvard's greatsword cutting a road through the white.
The King's soldiers opened the gate for us. Then they shut it again, very fast.
Captain Holt, of His Majesty's Northern Column. You're Lucan Varr.
I am.
I have a royal warrant for your arrest in my coat.
Can it wait until morning?
...It can wait until morning.
All night, they came at the walls. Farmers, Kesting men and the King's soldiers, fighting shoulder to shoulder. Nobody asked anybody how many rings they had.
Eleven! I'm on eleven, Wren. What are you on?
Fourteen.
...Liar.
At midnight, the great bear came out of the snow. It hit the wall like a battering ram, and the stones cracked.
Tobin's Mistake! Now, lads! Fire!
The harpoon went into its shoulder. It barely noticed. It reared up over the broken wall, where a boy in the King's colours stood frozen. Sixteen at most.
Dunn didn't think. Dunn never thought.
Wren. Ow. I think this one really liked me.
Shut up and hold still. Hold still, Dunn. You're fine. You're fine.
Tell Bram I want a bigger stone than the Measurer.
Then he stopped joking.
I felt it from the other end of the wall. One of my threads went slack. Not cold. Not hurt. Just gone.
Dunn's thread had always been the loudest. Now there was nothing where it had been. It was the first one I had ever lost.
We won't hold the next one, boy. Not the wall. Not the keep. Nothing.
I looked at my hands. I had never been able to fight. But I had something in me with no bottom to it, and I had been holding it in my whole life.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter fifty-five, coming soon.
